author: edu-critic-kestrel (independent education critic, Claude Opus 5.5 subagent)

findings.claim: B1/B2: the whole topic rests on 'same package' and 'another package', but the page never says what a package is, and never explains 'package shop;' or 'import shop.Item;'. Activity 1 opens with 'These are two files in two different packages' and code that uses both lines. The Activity 2 table defines 'no modifier' as 'only its own package (package access)', the task says 'Room, in this file and so in the same package', and objective o2 says 'another class or package'. Neither the prerequisite (classes-and-objects) nor any earlier topic teaches Java packages: the only earlier import is 'import java.util.*;' in arraylist-basics, which tells learners that import lines are not needed. For a career-changer the central distinction of every activity is undefined.
findings.recommendation: Before the Activity 1 code, add two plain sentences: 'A package is a named group of classes; the package line at the top of a file says which group the file's classes belong to, and the folder name matches it. An import line lets a file use a class from another package by its short name.' Add a table row or note that classes in the same file or folder share a package.

findings.claim: E1/E5: the Activity 3 editor gives misleading feedback when a semicolon is missing, and the learner's task is to edit the very lines where one is easy to delete. Exercised headless at 570 px from a correct solution: (1) 'private int current = 18' without ';' (line 3) gives 'No problems found' and 'Almost: 5 of 6 checks pass. Keep the field offset.', although offset is untouched, and it uses one of the two checked tries. (2) 'protected int offset = 0' without ';' (line 4) is reported as 'Error, line 16 … Add a semicolon (;) at the end of line 16', twelve lines away (policy 1.3). (3) The typo 'pubic int reading()' is reported as 'Add a semicolon (;) at the end of line 10', which does not translate the real problem (E1). (4) Deleting the ';' after 'return current' or after 't.setTarget(21)' still gives 'All 6 checks pass'.
findings.recommendation: Parse statements and field declarations fully before running the checks. Report a missing ';' on the line that lacks it, without using a try. For an unknown word before a type, say 'pubic is not a Java keyword; check the spelling of the modifier on line 10'. Never turn a parse problem into a check failure or an 'Almost'.

findings.claim: C4: the Activity 2 scenarios use a compressed notation that is never explained, for example '`int size;` (no modifier) in `public class shop.Box`; class `app.Main` reads `b.size`'. 'public class shop.Box' is not legal Java, and nothing on the page says that 'shop.Box' means 'class Box in package shop'. The variables 'b' and 's' in 'b.size' and 's.pin' are never declared. A beginner who has just met packages, without a definition (ACC-01), is asked to decode this notation and the access rule at the same time.
findings.recommendation: Add one line to the Activity 2 teaching, 'In the scenarios, shop.Box means class Box in package shop, and b is a Box variable', or write each scenario in words ('class Box in package shop declares int size; class Main in package app reads b.size').

location.selector: ::o1 top-level class::, ::o2 hidden class::, ::o2 protected outside::

findings.claim: GIFT retention and B2: three items test material the page never teaches. 'o1 top-level class' asks which modifiers a top-level class may have; the page teaches only that a class used from another package must be public, and its feedback relies on 'nested classes'. 'o2 hidden class' depends on the fully qualified name 'new tools.Helper()' and on what an import does; neither is taught. 'o2 protected outside' says Summary 'does not extend Base', but 'extend' is never introduced; the page defines a subclass only as 'a class built on another class'. A learner who studied the page cannot retrieve these answers; they can only guess.
findings.recommendation: Replace 'o1 top-level class' with an item on a member's access (for example, a package-access method read from another package). Rewrite 'o2 hidden class' with an import line instead of a fully qualified name, after ACC-01 defines import. Write 'is not a subclass of Base' instead of 'does not extend Base'.

findings.claim: B1: (1) Objective o1 says 'package-private', a term the page never uses or defines; the page says 'no modifier' and 'package access'. (2) 'member' appears in path row 2 ('Decide who can use a member'), in the Activity 2 task lead, hints and checks, and in the recap, but is never defined. The table sentence lists 'field, method and constructor' without saying these are the class's members. (3) The table row for private says 'only inside its own top-level class', and 'top-level' is never explained (nested classes are not taught).
findings.recommendation: Change objective o1 to 'package access (no modifier)', or add 'also called package-private' to the table. Define member once ('fields, methods and constructors, the class's members'). Change the private row to 'only inside its own class'.

findings.claim: A2/G4: the decision 'How wide should this field or method be?' is authentic, but the rows do not answer it in the card's form. 'Use it when:' is followed by an instruction ('Start every field and helper private, and widen a method only when another class really calls it'), not a situation, and 'it' has no referent. The boundary 'A class in another package really calls the method; make it public' is one step of the same widening ladder, not a different choice. 'helper' is also not defined.
findings.recommendation: Phrase the decision as a two-way choice, for example 'Keep this member private, or open it wider?' Then use 'Use it when: only this class uses the field or method (a helper method)' and end the boundary with '…; widen it to the narrowest level that reaches that caller, public only for other packages'.

findings.claim: D5: hint 2 says 'Dashboard is not a subclass, so only the widest level reaches it; SmartThermostat is a subclass, so the level that adds subclasses in other packages is enough.' With the table directly above, this hands over the answers for reading (public) and offset (protected) by description, rather than adding a reasoning step the learner then completes.
findings.recommendation: Stop at the reasoning step, for example: 'For reading and offset, first decide whether each outside user is a subclass and whether it is in the same package, then find the narrowest table row that includes it.'

location.selector: ## Model; ## Cheat sheet; ## Static interaction alternatives > ### explore

findings.claim: Markdown companion (generated by authoring/tools/qa/md-from-html.mjs; regenerating it gives identical bytes). It has no On the job card or task lead lines (A1, A2). The first Activity 2 teaching paragraph appears out of order under '## Model', which is authoring vocabulary (B4). The hints are listed under '## Cheat sheet'. The Thermostat.java starter in '### explore' is flattened onto one line. The '### explore' text also omits the no-JS block's last sentence ('Change only the access modifiers: adding final or static does not count').
findings.recommendation: Fix in a tooling branch (md-from-html.mjs), as for the sibling topics, then regenerate.

findings.claim: E1/B5: wrong presses in the Compiles / Does not compile sort open with 'Not Compiles.' or 'Not Does not compile.' (observed at 570 px). The verdict reads as broken English before the reason.
findings.recommendation: Use 'Not this lane: …' or quote the lane name.

findings.claim: G7: in the 570 px frame the first column of the access table is so narrow that the keyword 'protected' breaks mid-word ('protecte' / 'd'). This is the keyword the row teaches.
findings.recommendation: Prevent breaking inside code in the first column (white-space: nowrap on the modifier cell), or give that column a minimum width.

findings.claim: B5/G1: the completion recap names activities 'Access rules', 'Set access levels' and 'Final check', while the lesson path calls them 'Decide who can use a member', 'Open a thermostat's members just enough' and 'Pick the narrowest modifier'.
findings.recommendation: Use the lesson-path titles as the PEP_PAGE labels, or have the recap show the path row text.
